identity.instrumentFamily: Kang et al. 2020 Science Teaching Competence Self-Assessment (54 items / Appendix B)

construct.constructDefinition: Administrating assessment. Self-reported frequency of enacted teaching-related actions, mixed with self-perceived understanding and effectiveness; not observed teaching quality or student learning gains.

population.populationNotes: Original study: 210 South Korean primary/lower-secondary/upper-secondary science teachers. English publication wording; not the unprovided original Korean administration text. Project adult-teacher scope is not an author age boundary. No Chinese validation or local norms.

administration.timeFrame: General science teaching practice; no additional recall interval specified in the paper.
layoutConstraints: Appendix B factor membership and relative order retained; published English wording, not a claimed Korean or Chinese validated form.
Source methods §3.1: five response positions, 1=rarely and 5=always. Positions 2–4 retain numeric labels; intermediate verbal anchors were not published.
Independent administration is a project selection; use within the original 54-item context where possible. Factor structure does not establish standalone validity.
Complete-case arithmetic mean; any missing/invalid response yields no score. This missing policy is a disclosed project choice.
Estimated minutes are reading estimates, not measured administration times.

intendedUses.notes: Published factor grouping supports a research candidate; no standalone validation, diagnostic threshold, teacher ranking or causal learning inference.

localization.translationSource: Published English Appendix B in Kang et al. (2020); no translation of item text.
localization.notes: Typographic line-break hyphens and PDF ligatures normalized. No item translation or validated Chinese claim. English publication items may differ in administration language from the original Korean study.

items.content: In science class, I perform diagnostic assessments effectively to identify the starting point of student learning.
In science class, I perform formative assessments effectively to evaluate students’ academic achievement, improve teaching and learning, and provide feedback for students.
In science class, I perform summative assessments effectively to assess student achievement comprehensively.

scores.label: Administrating assessment
scores.description: Complete-case, equally weighted item mean (1–5). Higher means more frequent self-report, not verified effectiveness. No reverse-coded items in this retained positive-worded factor.

interpretations.headline: Administrating assessment: a record for reflection
interpretations.summary: This mean summarizes your own responses about administrating assessment. Higher values indicate more frequent self-report on the published response continuum; they do not establish the quality or effectiveness of your teaching. Statements about understanding and effectiveness remain personal judgments. The endpoints are 1 (rarely) and 5 (always); intermediate verbal labels were not published. The result is not a normative rank, proficiency level or diagnosis. A lower response may reflect limited opportunities or support as well as choices; a higher response does not show that students learned more.

guidance.text: What did one recent assessment tell you that you could actually use to adjust teaching?
Use one brief diagnostic or formative task, change one next step in response, and check understanding again. Record the change rather than treating more testing as better teaching.

limitations: Original study context: South Korean school science teachers; English publication wording is not a validated Chinese translation or independently validated standalone factor.
No normative comparison, cutoff, teacher ranking, causal attribution or cross-factor/global total.
A score is produced only when every item in this factor has a valid response. Missing or unavailable evidence is not zero; no imputation or prorating.
The methods describe five frequency response positions and endpoint words only; intermediate numeric labels are a disclosed presentation choice.
report.disclaimer: For teacher research and voluntary professional reflection. No diagnosis, appraisal, promotion or student-learning conclusion. If responses or evidence are insufficient, do not infer low competency.

instruction.source: Project presentation instruction based on source methods §3.1, not a quotation of an unpublished original survey introduction.
instruction.text: Reflect on how often these statements describe your science teaching-related actions. Select one of five response positions: 1 = rarely; 5 = always. Intermediate positions are shown as numbers because their verbal labels are not specified in the publication. This is a research reflection record, not a teacher performance evaluation. Items about understanding or effectiveness reflect your own judgment, not an independently tested ability.
